channel.title: European Medical Journal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from European Medical Journal (emjreviews.com)

item.title: Microneedle Patches May Improve Hyperpigmentation Treatment
item.description: Microneedle patches may improve hyperpigmentation treatment with better skin delivery and minimal side effects. Read more.

item.title: COVID-19 Outcomes in Cystic Fibrosis Transplants
item.description: Lung function may shape COVID-19 outcomes in cystic fibrosis transplant recipients. Learn more about the latest findings and clinical implications.

item.title: Hideki Garren on rethinking multiple sclerosis care
item.description: Hideki Garren explores how our understanding of MS is evolving, the challenge of measuring disease progression and what the future holds.

item.title: Nanotechnology Therapeutics Reframe Autoimmune Disease Care
item.description: Nanotechnology therapeutics may reshape autoimmune disease care with targeted delivery and immune modulation. Read more.

item.title: ABPI calls for NHS data use to boost trial recruitment
item.description: The NHS is sitting on a gold mine of patient data that could, in the ABPI’s view, help rescue the UK’s faltering clinical trials sector.

item.title: Liquid Biopsy Accelerates Diagnosis of Burkitt’s Lymphoma
item.description: Liquid biopsy enables faster, accurate diagnosis of Burkitt’s lymphoma in low-resource settings. Learn how this approach could transform care.

item.title: Low Testosterone Tied to Extreme Prostate Cancer Progression
item.description: Read more about how low testosterone levels are linked to ‘extreme’ disease progression in patients with prostate cancer under active surveillance.

item.title: Childhood Trauma Tied to Increased Dementia Risk
item.description: Discover more about how childhood adversities are linked to faster ageing-related changes, including an increased risk of dementia.

item.title: Type 1 Diabetes Tied to Threefold Increase in Dementia Risk
item.description: Adults above 50 with Type 1 diabetes are nearly three times as likely to develop incident dementia as those without. Read more.

item.title: CKD Severity Linked to Increased Risk of Cognitive Impairment
item.description: EMCKD severity is linked to cognitive impairment risk, with proteinuria a key predictor. Learn more about the findings from this large cohort study.
